assumptions_resolved: The migration schema of 2026-09-05 was used as the authority throughout; the 2026-08-19 CSV was consulted only for the ingest/ignore rulings it still owns.

The loader carries its own psql invocation with ON_ERROR_STOP and no outer transaction wrapper, so each window's SQL owns its BEGIN/COMMIT and atomicity is not a side effect of how the helper was invoked.
Both workflows require an explicitly named database secret and refuse to run without it. No connection string is assembled from a project ref.
No database was contacted from this session and neither loader was run against a live target. The transaction shape is proven by asserting on the generated SQL, not by executing it.
sync-masters.mjs was not built, as the contract prohibits; the masters half of Step 7 remains open.

The governed review at head 71f31a32 returned REVISE with five findings. Four were real and are fixed with a regression test each: a whitespace-only numeric field became a real zero, the component reconcile compared floating point sums exactly, the resume read interpolated the company code into SQL unquoted, and a one-sided invoice list was dropped without a mismatch flag. The fifth, a group-key collision in the production projection, was not reachable because the line hash is part of that key; the separator was still made consistent with the order path and the reason is recorded in the code rather than in a test that cannot fail.

The governed review at head 7002542d confirmed the four round-one fixes and returned REVISE on one blocking design defect: the scheduled sync selected the window CONTAINING today, so each seven-day window would have been fetched and SEALED on its first day, discarding the remaining six days of orders while the ledger reported the window complete. Both entry points now select only windows that have CLOSED, the backfill clamps a future --to rather than obeying it, and the helper that returned the containing window was deleted rather than left available. Tests now assert the open/closed boundary itself, which no test did before -- the reason the defect survived two earlier reviews. The reviewer's minor note is also fixed: a negative or fractional --limit reached slice(0, -1) and silently dropped the last outstanding pair.
